metadata.layer: Layer 3G — FaunaTech Ecological Trait Alignment, Tamil Nadu Megalithic Graffiti Complexity Control, & Gulf Seals Audit

confounder_audit_motif_vs_object_type.interpretation: SEVERE artifact-type confounding exists across fauna motifs (e.g., Gavi/Fish are 94-100% on TAB:B/I tablets; Hare is 92% on TAB:C copper tablets; Bull1/Zebu/Buff/Tigr are 80-91% on SEAL:S seals). Uncontrolled trait tests therefore mix fauna semantics with object-type vocabulary — making within-object-type stratification and species-level permutation mandatory.

gadd_1932.citation: C. J. Gadd (1932). 'Seals of Ancient Indian Style Found at Ur'. Proceedings of the British Academy, Vol. 18, pp. 191-210.
gadd_1932.notes: Includes Gadd No. 1 (U.7683 / BM 120573, Indus bull iconography with cuneiform 'sag-ku-zi', NOT Indus script), several uninscribed/iconographic Gulf-style seals, and a subset of circular/square seals bearing authentic Indus script.

laursen_2010.citation: Steffen Terp Laursen (2010). 'The westward transmission of Indus Valley sealing technology: origin and development of the "Gulf Type" seal and other administrative technologies in Early Dilmun, c. 2100-2000 BC'. Arabian Archaeology and Epigraphy 21: 96-134.

A. Parpola, B. M. Pande & P. Koskikallio (2010, 2019, 2022, forthcoming). Corpus of Indus Seals and Inscriptions (CISI) Vol. 3: Part 1 (2010), Part 2 (2019), Part 3 (2022 Indo-Iranian Borderlands), Part 4 (planned: Persian Gulf & West Asia).
parpola_cisi_vol3_and_syntheses.estimated_worldwide_west_asia_inscribed_: 30-40 total (comprising ~28 circular Gulf-type seals with Indus script plus ~10-12 classic square Harappan / cylinder seals from Ur, Kish, Tell Asmar, Nippur, Tello/Girsu, Umma, Susa, Tepe Yahya, Salut, Ra's al-Junayz, Gonur Depe, Shortughai, Altyn Depe).

gap_vs_layer4b_percolation_threshold.honest_verdict: Adding the remaining ~5-15 published Gulf/Mesopotamian circular seals from Gadd (1932), Laursen (2010; 28 inscribed Gulf Type seals), and CISI Vol. 3.4 (forthcoming) would bring our Gulf constraint graph from E=23 to at most E=28-38 — STILL 35-45 circular seals SHORT of Layer 4B's m*=50 additional (73 total) percolation threshold EVEN WITH k=2 bilingual anchors, and >165 seals short without a bilingual (k=0, m*>180). Exhausting all currently published West Asian seals cannot break the phonetic identifiability barrier; newly excavated seals or a genuine bilingual remain mandatory.
